description:
Create an order from the session cart (starts unpaid — PENDING_ARTWORK
or PENDING_PAYMENT depending on the server).

For a one-line cart, pass that line's `offer_id` alone. For a cart with
several lines, pass `selections=[{line_id, offer_id}, ...]`, one per line,
to order them together as one order with one item per line; a bare
`offer_id` against such a cart is rejected (`MultiLineCartError`) rather
than silently ordering just one line.
Each item re-sends the sku + configuration its quote priced and binds the
chosen offer; the server recomputes price, so no money is sent. Every
`offer_id` must belong to the cart (`OfferNotFoundError` / `LineNotFoundError`
otherwise — re-run `order_get_quote`). If RendReal refuses the chosen offer, the
job fails with `OfferRefusedError` and no order is placed: quote again and let the
customer choose. If RendReal refuses the order itself, the job fails with
`OrderRefusedError`: the refusal is permanent, so offer a change to the setup or
customer support, never a retry.

Shipping and tax are filled by Stripe at checkout. Attach artwork per line:
with `selections`, set each entry's `design_id` + `design_snapshot_id`; with a
bare `offer_id`, pass the top-level `design_id` + `design_snapshot_id`. Both
ids are required for a design to attach, and the snapshot must be the owned
design's latest. Every line needs artwork — a design, or a finished artwork file
uploaded via `order_get_artwork_upload_page` — before the order can be paid
(`order_create_payment_link` enforces it).

A line already ordered in this session is refused (`LineAlreadyOrderedError`)
before any upstream order is placed, so the same still-quoted line can't be
bought twice; `order_view_cart` marks such a line `in_checkout=true`.
Start a new line to buy it again.

If `catalog_configure_product` reported an Unmet Constraint for any selected
line, the order is refused (`UnmetConstraintUnansweredError`; `detail.lines`
lists every such line with its asks in `unmet`) until the customer answers for
each listed line. Tell the customer, per line, what they asked for and what the
option accepts. If they accept every listed line as configured, call again with
`unmet_accepted=true`, which orders all the selected lines. If they want a change
on any line, call `catalog_configure_product` with their answer for that line
instead.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED for the `order_id` and each line's
`item_id`. Then get any missing artwork: design it against the order, or have
the customer upload a finished file. Call `order_create_payment_link`
only when the customer asks to pay.
An item with `designable: false` cannot be designed here: for that item offer
only the upload of a finished print file, never a design.
name: order_create

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Place the order
